author: Thomas Hurley
title: Recaptured: 'School of Rock,' Big Bite Night and Malcolm Todd
text:
Welcome to Recaptured — a weekly roundup of The Daily’s photojournalism, featuring our reporters’ most memorable moments. This week’s Recaptured includes concerts in Chicago, festivals in Evanston and animal blessings.
A few weeks ago, The Daily went looking for things that cost less than $20 at the Evanston Farmers’ Market. We found pastries at Aficionadough, sauce at Tasting India and tiles at Tina Kalil Tile & Clay, to name a few. (Chris Qin/The Daily Northwestern ) A crowd of Evanston residents enjoyed a performance from five-time Grammy-nominated singer Justin Roberts, optional blessings for their pets and free food from local restaurants at the first-ever Fall Fest on Oct. 4. (Glennis Woosley/The Daily Northwestern) Indie-rock band Mt. Joy performed on Oct. 3 at Huntington Bank Pavilion at Northerly Island. In an era of heavily-produced records, intricate set pieces and flashy singles, Mt. Joy stands out as unequivocally human and relatable. (Nora Ahearn/The Daily Northwestern) Audience members from Evanston to New York packed Cahn Auditorium for a staged reading of “October 7: In Their Words” last Tuesday night. The show, sponsored by Northwestern Hillel, was created by the Unreported Story Society, a conservative media company led by filmmakers Phelim McAleer and Ann McElhinney. (Clara B. Freeth/The Daily Northwestern) The Wildcats dominated Ball State with a season-high 45 points last Saturday — including a pick-six by redshirt senior defensive back Robert Fitzgerald and a 19-yard touchdown by senior wide receiver Griffin Wilde. (Xuan Day Tran/The Daily Northwestern) Arts Alliance brought a dramatic, high-energy production of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s “School of Rock” to Shanley Pavilion across four performances last Friday and Saturday. (Christina Lin/The Daily Northwestern) The Chicks, formerly known as The Dixie Chicks, stopped in Chicago on Oct. 3 and 4 for their tour celebrating the 20th anniversary of their seventh studio album, “Taking the Long Way,” which topped the Billboard 200 chart in 2006 and won five Grammys. (Lydia Park/The Daily Northwestern) No. 1 Northwestern defeated No. 6 Iowa in a conference clash at Lakeside Field on Friday, earning its 600th program victory. Senior forward Ashley Sessa scored both goals for the home side, her tenth and eleventh of the year. (Joseph Trevisani/The Daily Northwestern) With purple wristbands and maps in hand, Northwestern students explored Downtown Evanston for free bites on Oct. 4. The annual Big Bite Night featured 23 local businesses, each setting up tables and signs inviting students to try out their menus. (Iris Yu/The Daily Northwestern) Email: photo@dailynorthwestern.com
